reasoning.local_section: The equilateral three-phasor zero has full two-dimensional Jacobian rank, and fixing the third phase leaves determinant sqrt(3)/18, so the inverse-function theorem supplies a smooth local right inverse.
reasoning.global_obstruction: Boundary triangle equality forces every ordered unit phasor to equal the unit boundary value. Each component would have winding one, but any circle-valued component extending over a disk must have boundary winding zero.
reasoning.fixed_chart_control: At z=-r the fixed-r chart requires a two-phasor sum of modulus four although its maximum is two.
reasoning.gauge_custody: Distinct equilateral triples decode to the same zero amplitude while their actual carrier cells differ, so amplitude alone cannot restore both actual gauge states.

ceiling_caveat: The argument covers finite ordered unit-phasor arithmetic means. It does not cover weighted or nonmean encodings, discontinuous sections, stateful reversible gauge transport, conserved phase geometries, or general phase couplers.
winding_sample_role: The 64-point calculation is a reproducibility witness; the analytic boundary-degree argument supports the global claim.
